chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has four wives, and he spends the night with three of them during their nights and touches them, but when he sleeps with the fourth one during her night, he does not touch her. Is there any sin upon him in this? He said: 'He is only required to be with her during her night and remain with her until morning, and he is not required to have intercourse with her if he does not desire that.'
ai.seo_question: What are the marital rights and obligations regarding night distribution and intercourse for a man with four wives in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic distinction between the obligatory share of time (*qismah*) and the recommended act of intimacy (*mu'asharah*) in polygyny. He establishes that while a husband must physically reside with each wife for a night and the following morning to fulfill the equity requirement, sexual intercourse remains discretionary (*mubah*) rather than compulsory, reflecting the Shia emphasis on fairness in presence over mandatory consummation.
